findings.title: Send and Make public call the user's payment key under someone else's stake key "your own public account: it comes back", where the sign window says its staking rewards aren't yours
findings.scenario: A stranger reads the user's Receive address (0/0) on chain and pays 1 ₳ to base(that payment key hash, the stranger's own stake key hash). The wallet counts the UTxO, and UTxO details calls it "Your receive address, the one Receive shows" with a Copy button (e9a#3). The user copies the address from there to gather their ADA and pays it 20,000 ₳ with the public Send, or makes their private balance public to it with Max. destination.ts ownAccount runs is_own_address, which checks the payment key alone, and returns own: true, account: active. carriesStakeKey is false (the stake part is the stranger's), so staked is undefined. The form and the review show OwnNote, "This is your own public account: it comes back, less the fee." (Make public: "This is your own public account: anyone can link it…"), and Total leaving counts only the fee. The signed transaction pays the 20,000 ₳ to an address whose stake credential is the stranger's. Until the wallet next spends that UTxO, the stake counts for the stranger's pool and the rewards go to the stranger's reward account: about 40 ₳ a month at 2.5% a year. The next public payment takes it first, since it's the largest pure-ADA UTxO, and its change goes back to 0/0. The connector reads the same shape the other way: an output there in a site's transaction is listed as paid, with "It pays your payment key with a stake part that isn't yours, counted as leaving. You can still spend it, but its staking rewards aren't yours." No ADA is lost: the UTxO stays in the balance and spendable.
findings.since: bbde3418 (2026-09-27, privacy review §2.17: own by payment key, whatever the staking part; in 1.0.0). Send's own-account note from 7b6db25c/d423b79a.
findings.evidence: wasm/src/lib.rs:5088-5131 is_own_address: "under one of its payment keys, whatever its staking part (an enterprise address, say), as the wallet counts and spends the account". It returns true on a payment-key match and never looks at the delegation part. wasm/tests/api_test.rs:2916 knows_the_accounts_own_addresses_by_payment_key_too pins it: "Receive 0's key with someone else's stake key" is own. extension/src/background/destination.ts:119-124: `own: keys.cardano.isOwnAddress(address, found?.keys ?? [])`, `staked: keys.cardano.carriesStakeKey(address)`. destination.ts:126 returns {own:true, account} first. destination.ts:65-70 maps that to {own, ownAccount}. ui/screens/CardanoSend.tsx:295-297 shows OwnNote in the form. :164-171 leaving and tokenKinds skip `p.own && p.ownAccount === active`. :233-243 shows OwnNote in the review. en.json:1798 send.warn.ownAccount: "This is your own public account: it comes back, less the fee." Withdraw.tsx:249-250 and :317 OwnWarning; en.json:3018. In contrast, wasm/src/cip30.rs:499-511 own_address needs `(Key(h), Key(stake)) if *stake == self.stake`. :1396-1408 lists the payment key under another stake part as paid with own_payment_key. DappApprovals.tsx:1180-1184 adds the warning; en.json:444 and :518. Transaction details agrees with the review, not the window: tx-view.ts:278 and :316 markYours sets yours {kind:"account"} by payment key alone, which TxDetail shows as "Yours, in your public account" (en.json:2885). flows.md:227 documents only "by its payment key, never by its stake key alone". The planted address's source is Utxos.tsx:411 (e9a#3).
findings.fix: Keep `own` as it is for the balance and for Make public's re-linking warning: §2.17 is right that the payment key alone links the money. Add the fact the connector already uses: whether the address's stake part is the account's own stake key (`carriesStakeKey` is that test). When it isn't (another stake key, a pointer, or none), the Send and Make public notes say the payment key is the user's but the stake part isn't, so its staking rewards aren't the user's, in dappUi.warn.ownKey's sense, rather than only "it comes back". Total leaving can stay as it is. The same class: e9a#3's UTxO details words, and tx-view.ts markYours (278, 316), which should say the stake part isn't the user's for such an output. Test: resolveDestination of base(receive 0's key, foreign stake) gives own true plus a stake-elsewhere flag, and the CardanoSend review renders the new line, not send.warn.ownAccount alone.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md, archive/plans/*.md, privacy.md, flows.md and keys-and-accounts.md for "stake part that isn't", ownPaymentKey, own_payment_key, "someone else's stake key", "whatever its staking part", "comes back, less the fee" and §2.17. privacy-review §2.17 (bbde341) made own mean the payment key, for Make public's re-linking warning. #359 fixed the reverse shape (a stranger's key under our stake key). backlog.md:156 is about a wallet key's hash in a stake position, a different shape. e9a#3 has the same root on the UTxO details screen, but its fix doesn't reach the Send and Make public reviews or Transaction details. Nothing records it.

findings.title: The sign window says a site's payment into a Seedelf hides whose it is without checking its register: a register written as found shows on chain whose it is
findings.scenario: A site builds a transaction that pays 25 ₳ of the account's into Seedelf Wallet's contract. Its inline datum is the recipient Seedelf's own datum, copied byte for byte from the UTxO holding its token, with no re-randomization: d = 1, the README's "bad d value". A naive "pay a Seedelf name" integration writes exactly this. inspect reads two 48-byte points (register_datum), is_payable holds, and the output gets seedelf = "register". The window lists "Seedelf Wallet's contract" with the privacy callout "It pays a Seedelf. Nothing on chain says whose, but it comes from your public account in the open.", and privacy.md:336 promises "whose owner stays hidden". On chain the output's datum equals the Seedelf UTxO's, so anyone reading the contract can see which Seedelf it pays. The wallet's own contract scan keeps every Seedelf's register. Every later spend of that output shows the Seedelf's owner spending it, and whatever is spent beside it. When the Seedelf is the user's own (a site that "moves money to your Seedelf"), the public account, that Seedelf and the new private UTxO are tied together for anyone to see. A register copied from any earlier contract UTxO (two UTxOs with one register) does the same. No money is lost; the window's privacy line is false.
findings.since: fe8b7748 (chunk 15, the classification; in 1.0.0); the callout's words since 7cc3f363 (2026-10-02)
findings.evidence: wasm/src/cip30.rs:998-1002: is_register_datum is register_datum plus is_payable. cip30.rs:1384-1395: `Address::Shelley(s) if *s.payment().as_hash() == contract_hash => Some(if inline…is_register_datum {"register"} else {"none"})`. Nothing compares the register with any register already on chain. ui/screens/DappApprovals.tsx:1190-1194 shows dappUi.privacy.paysSeedelfAccount (or …Session). en.json:467: "It pays a Seedelf. Nothing on chain says whose, but it comes from your public account in the open." privacy.md:336 says "under a register (a Seedelf payment, whose owner stays hidden, …)". ui/dapp.ts:128-137 signingTies(seedelf) only drops "Your private balance isn't in it". The wallet's own payments never write a register as found: seedelf-core/src/build.rs:336-340 deposit_output re-randomizes, pinned by wasm/tests/api_test.rs:1941 the_cardano_account_pays_someones_seedelf_under_a_fresh_copy_of_its_register. privacy.md:77 and chunk-09-transfer.md:70 state the rule. The root README.md:167 lists "A bad d value" among the known de-anonymizing attacks. The worker already has what a check needs: background/contract-scan.ts:78-84, where Locator.register keeps every Seedelf's register in the kept contract view. decode.rs register_detail marks only payable or dead, and tx-view.ts markYours marks only ownership.
findings.fix: Say only what's checked. The worker has every Seedelf's register in the kept contract view (no request) and the wallet's own UTxOs' registers. Compare each paid register with them, and optionally every contract UTxO the view holds. When one matches, replace "Nothing on chain says whose" with a warning that this register is already on chain, so anyone can see whose Seedelf it pays (new .warn./.privacy. words). Without a kept view, the window shouldn't claim the owner stays hidden. Change privacy.md:336 to match. Fix it in the same match as w2#2 (a key address with the contract's hash) and d1#3 (a dead or hashed register), at cip30.rs:1385. Test: a site transaction paying the contract under the inline datum of a Seedelf in the contract view. Today paid[0].seedelf is "register" and the window shows paysSeedelfAccount.
findings.owner_why: The fix adds a warning to the sign window and changes what privacy.md promises about a site's Seedelf payment. The owner chooses between checking the kept view and warning, or only softening the line.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md, archive/plans/*.md and privacy.md for re-random, "as found", "same register", "bad d", "root datum", paysSeedelf and copied. Hits: only the wallet's own rule (privacy.md:77, chunk-09-transfer.md:70) and the README's "bad d value" attack. d1#3 and w2#2 cover other mislabels in the same match, not a register copied as found.

findings.title: The sign window leaves out "It carries metadata" whenever a note is shown, so a site's other metadata beside a CIP-20 note is never mentioned
findings.scenario: A site's transaction carries the CIP-20 note "Thanks for order 77" (label 674's msg). Under label 1337 it also carries {"email": "alice@example.com", "order": 77}, or other keys under 674 beside msg, as Minswap writes its extraData. The body commits to all of it through auxiliary_data_hash. inspect's note_of gives metadata = true plus the note lines. The window shows "Its note, which anyone can read" with the note, but its notes list skips "It carries metadata, which anyone can read." because there is a note. The user signs a transaction that publishes data the window never named, tied to their public account for good; only Transaction details shows it. No money moves.
findings.evidence: wasm/src/cip30.rs:1033-1066: note_of returns `(!metadata.is_empty(), note)`, one flag for any label. :1770-1773 sets TxSummary.metadata, documented "Any metadata at all" (:915-916). DappApprovals.tsx:1083: `if (s.metadata && !s.note) notes.push(tr("dappUi.note.metadata"))`. :1279-1286 renders the note. en.json:414 dappUi.itsNote = "Its note, which anyone can read"; :426 dappUi.note.metadata = "It carries metadata, which anyone can read." archive/plans/chunk-17-transaction-view.md:214-215 records that Minswap's swap carries msg beside its own extraData under 674, so honest transactions have this shape too. tests/dapp-prompt.test.ts's fixture has metadata: false, and no test pins a note together with other metadata.
findings.fix: Have note_of report whether there's anything beyond the note's msg lines (another label, or another key under 674), for example `other_metadata: bool`. Show the metadata line ("It carries other metadata too, which anyone can read") whenever that's true, note or not. Test: inspect_tx of a transaction with 674 {msg} and 721 {…}. Today the window's notes have no metadata line.
findings.known_check: I searched backlog.md and archive/plans/*.md for metadata together with note, "carries metadata" and dappUi.note.metadata. chunk-17 records reading the note beside Minswap's extraData, but nothing about the window's line. e3a#3/e3b#1 concern the note's own text and its hash, not other labels.

guards.stops: check_paths: signing for, or spending, a public-account UTxO whose address doesn't carry the payment key its path derives on this network. So an account switch between readAccount and the build fails rather than mixing one account's UTxOs and stake state with another's keys.
guards.test: wasm/tests/api_test.rs:257, :374, :723, :1279 ('is not under the account's payment key')

guards.stops: account_send zips the request's payments with built.paid in order, so each review row's amount and minimum belong to its own recipient (send.ts:166 then zips destinations[i] in the same order)
guards.test: wasm/tests/api_test.rs sends_to_several_addresses_in_one_payment (~628: 'Both payments, in order, then the change to 0/0')

guards.stops: account_send_many refuses an unpayable address (check_payable) or a register a payment would be lost under (check_register / is_payable) before building

account_payment refuses a picked token the eligible UTxOs don't hold, or more of it than they hold, so the echoed request tokens a review shows are exactly what the outputs carry (each_tokens = asked.min(held))
Every deposit output (move-in, a Send to a Seedelf, change into the contract) goes under a fresh re-randomization of the owner's register, never the register as found
The staking patch (certificates, withdrawal, votes) is refused after signing, so the signature covers the patched body the review was built from
The CIP-20 note patch is refused after signing, and over a body that already has metadata
guards.test: none that isolates it (note_test.rs:211 fails at the metadata guard first, per R2b)

guards.stops: own_address: a site's output counts as the account's (not leaving) only with an in-range payment key AND the account's stake key. Its key under any other stake part is listed as paid and warned about.
A payment or DRep key never signs over an input or collateral the wallet couldn't find, so nothing outside the summary's net is spent
sign_tx re-runs inspect over the same request string the window was read from, and refuses one that needs others' signatures without partialSign: what's signed is what was shown
With the account's collateral in it, a collateral return to anyone else is refused (and :1330, one marked to fail), so 'collateral at risk' is the account's exact loss
At approval, the signature is made with the keys of the account the request was read for (withViewKeys), after stillConnected, heldForLovejoin, keptApart and sameAccount are checked again
Send, Create, Collateral and staking submit only the kept transaction with the reviewed hash on this network, within its TTL; a sent one is never rebuilt
guards.test: tests/transfer.test.ts 'refuses to send anything but the reviewed transaction'; tests/staking.test.ts:701-717

guards.stops: Make private submits only the reviewed move-in (hash, network), refuses one older than 10 minutes, and sends a maybe-sent one's same bytes again
guards.test: tests/move-in.test.ts 'refuses to send anything but the reviewed transaction'

guards.stops: The collateral payment's output #0 (the 5 ₳; payments come before change in build_account_payment and patches don't reorder) is recorded as the collateral on the account its review was built on
guards.test: tests/coin-control.test.ts 'is recorded on the account it was built on, and pays, whichever is active when Send returns'

guards.stops: Total leaving counts every payment and token except those to the active account's own address, plus the fee; another of the user's accounts and a stranger's key under our stake key count as leaving
guards.test: tests/screens-wiring-review-fixes.test.ts ('counts the payment and its token as leaving')

checked_ok: Public Send, recipients: each review row (address, $handle and its address, or a Seedelf's tag and whole name) is the worker's resolved destination. WebAssembly pays `d.seedelf?.name ?? d.address`, the same value, and `Paid` carries no address, so `...p` can't override what's shown (send.ts:124-129 and 163-169, rpc.ts:729-733).

Public Send, amounts: each amount is built.paid[i] in request order (lib.rs:1716-1727). The tokens echo the request, and build_account_payment pays exactly those, because asks are checked against the same eligible set the mandatory inputs are drawn from (build.rs:887-900, 971-991). Token rows take the held token's Koios decimals, as the form parsed them.

Public Send, totals: Total leaving = Σ payments not to the active account's own address + fee. After = Home's total − leaving, which is right because Home's total holds the rewards a withdrawal moves into change. Max pays total − fee − the change floor. RewardsRow shows the withdrawal the build signed (withdrawing → sign_staking).

Public Send, note: the review shows Note::text (trimmed). The transaction carries the same text, split into lines of at most 64 bytes, with aux hash = hash_cbor of the encoding written (note.rs:51-110).
Public Send: change always goes to the active account's 0/0 (lib.rs:1696). An account switch between readAccount and the build fails check_paths and never mixes accounts.

Public Send to a Seedelf: the worker's view gives the UTxO holding that name, own Seedelfs are refused (send.ts:177-182), and WebAssembly re-checks the UTxO and is_payable. The output goes under a fresh re-randomization, so 'the chain doesn't show it's theirs' holds for the wallet's own payments.

Make private: 'Into' = built.lovelace (the sum over deposit outputs), tokens = built.tokens (what's actually paid), Total leaving = lovelace + fee, private after = private + lovelace. Each deposit is under a fresh register; 'links your public account … not to any Seedelf name' holds.

Account-paid mint: Locked = seedelf_minimum_lovelace, the Seedelf output's own lovelace. The name is the minted token name, and the fee is the settled ScriptFee.total. The draft and the finish re-randomize but select the same inputs, so the reviewed name is the one minted. The collateral returns to its own address, less 3/2 of the fee.

Collateral: To, Address and Set aside are the 5 ₳ output to the account's own 0/0. Output #0 is that payment (Payee::Address with no tokens is one output; change follows). The only signed part the review omits is the rewards withdrawal (e8b#2).

Staking: every StakingReview figure comes from WebAssembly's StakingResult (pool, drep, deposit, drepDeposit, refund, withdrawal, fee), and the after row is right for each action. Staking.tsx build() captures the action and the chosen pool or DRep in one call, so the name shown and the certificate built can't come apart (unlike e7a#1's swap). DRep retire's own-vote move uses the same fresh read WebAssembly builds with.

Sign window: every figure comes from one inspect of one request string. Approval re-runs inspect over that string and signs the same body hash; ties() only adds `yours`. The net counts the fee, deposits, donation and proposal deposits as leaving, and the account's withdrawals and refunds as put in. Collateral at risk = put up − returned to the account. Expires rounds up and reads 'Never' past Date's range.

Sign window, ties(): traced against address shapes. The site account's own inputs tie nothing. base(another account's key, any stake) ties that account. base(stranger, another account's stake) is `staked`. Our key under a stranger's stake gets no `yours` and reads 'Your payment key, with a stake part that isn't yours'. A pool's reward account that is the site account's own stake key is excluded, and that only benefits the user.

signData: the address shown is DataFor::shown() of the same DataFor whose bytes go in the COSE protected header, and the key named is the one that signs (cip30.rs:2205-2220, 2320-2345). A DRep's ID or enterprise address is only taken with governance.

Transaction details (decode.rs): shows every body field, including unknown keys. It marks required signers that are the user's, checks the metadata hash, and hashes the same raw body bytes the window's txHash names, so waitingCbor hands it the waiting request's own bytes.

Validity window: the wallet's own public transactions carry tip + 7200 slots (account.ts validUntil), held for 10 minutes between Review and Send. A site's 'Valid from' shows only while it's still to come.
notes: For e9a#3: the same root (own = payment key alone, any stake part) appears on two more screens. Send's and Make public's own-account notes (x1a#1) and Transaction details' markYours (tx-view.ts:278, :316: 'Yours, in your public account') both call base(our key, a stranger's stake) the user's public account. The connector's own_address (cip30.rs:503) calls the same shape 'a stake part that isn't yours… its staking rewards aren't yours'. Fixing e9a#3's words alone leaves the other two.

For e9a#2: in the sign window (DappApprovals.tsx:1035, tokenDecimals without Koios's decimals), raw units overstate what the account gets as well as what it sends. A site whose own page says 'you get 1,000,000 FOO' matches the window, while Home then shows 1 FOO (6 decimals from Koios). The 'not on the wallet's list' mark is shown beside it, which softens this.

For X2 and the owner (private side, not traced through select_script_inputs' order): x1a#2's shape can also come from a stranger. A stranger can pay the user's Seedelf under that Seedelf's own register as found (d = 1, the README's 'bad d value', about 1.5 ₳). That UTxO is owned (is_owned holds), so it sits in the private balance classed received:<tx> (shared/histories.ts). Every spend of it shows on chain that it's that Seedelf owner's. mint.ts's header says a stealth mint 'takes received money first', so this UTxO may be exactly what ties a new stealth Seedelf to the one the stranger paid, against CreateSeedelf's 'Only money others paid you keeps the Seedelf apart from your public account'. The README lists the attack, but the wallet's balance reading doesn't flag the shape, though contract-scan's kept view has every Seedelf's register to compare with.

For the owner: the sign window names a site's DRep votes by a shortened action ID only (DappApprovals.tsx:1256-1266, shortHex(txHash, 8, 4)#index). A site given governance can vote the user's DRep on a different action than its own page describes, and the window offers no title to check. The wallet's Governance page reads titles, cached for an hour, so it could show one without a request. Not a finding, since the ID shown is the one signed.

Nit: an old-style StakeRegistration of the account's own key (cert 0, no deposit field) is said as 'registers your stake key' with no figure (ui/dapp.ts:201-215, Cert.deposit None), while the window's total counts the implicit key_deposit as leaving.

For the owner, consistency only (R2a's is_payable note): the sign window's 'register' class accepts a register whose discrete log is public (u = g, x = 1). A site can write one, and anyone can take what's paid there, yet the window says 'It pays a Seedelf'. The amount leaving is shown, and the user loses nothing beyond a site paying itself.

Minor, in e3a#3/e3b#1's family: waitingCbor returns the first waiting request whose summary has that hash. Two requests with the same body but different auxiliary data (only one matching auxiliary_data_hash) share a hash, so Transaction details for the second shows the first one's bytes and metadata.

Contrived, so not reported: Send's own check also ignores a stake part that is another of the user's accounts. base(the active account's key, Account 2's stake key) gets only 'This is your own public account: it comes back' and no warning that the address ties the two accounts. Building such an address needs both keys.
